stages.title: SIXTH-CENTURY BCE SETTING: CITIES, STATES AND INTELLECTUAL FERMENT — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Memory hook: C-K-R: Cities, Kings, Renunciants - plus the caveat 'context is not cause alone'.
stages.mechanism: Memory hook: C-K-R: Cities, Kings, Renunciants - plus the caveat 'context is not cause alone'.
stages.consequence: These conditions widened their audience, but doctrine cannot be mechanically derived from iron or trade.
stages.trap: QUALIFICATION: The subcontinent did not urbanize uniformly, merchants were not the only followers, and economic change cannot explain specific doctrines such as anatta or anekantavada.
stages.answer: FACT: Upinder Singh's useful frame is 'cities, kings and renunciants' for north India c.

stages.title: THE SHRAMANA FIELD: HETERODOXY WITHOUT A FALSE BINARY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Parivrajaka denotes a wandering renunciant; shramana a striver/ascetic across several non-Vedic movements; upasaka/upasika a Buddhist lay follower.
stages.mechanism: Mains/PYQ use: A comparison answer should begin with the common debate field and then separate ontology, path and institution.
stages.consequence: Correct: Jainism and Buddhism retained them but interpreted them differently.
stages.trap: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.answer: 'Shramana versus Brahmana' is a useful contrast of authority and practice, but historical interaction was continuous.

stages.title: PRE-MAHAVIRA JAIN TRADITION AND THE TIRTHANKARAS — [CORE PRELIMS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Mains/PYQ use: Use a graded evidence ladder: sacred sequence - plausible Parshva memory - firmer Mahavira horizon.
stages.mechanism: Jain tradition presents a succession of twenty-four Tirthankaras, with Mahavira as the twenty-fourth.
stages.consequence: LIMIT: Iconographic or literary references to earlier Tirthankaras do not prove the historicity or traditional dates of all twenty-four.
stages.trap: FACT: A Tirthankara is a 'ford-maker' who discovers and teaches a route across bondage; the term is not a creator-god title.
stages.answer: Historical confidence is unequal: Parshvanatha is the strongest pre-Mahavira candidate, while claims for very early figures belong primarily to sacred tradition.

stages.title: MAHAVIRA: TRADITIONAL BIOGRAPHY AND HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Pali Buddhist texts know him as Nigantha Nataputta, proving that an organized Nigantha/Jain community was recognized by rival near-contemporary traditions.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Pali Buddhist texts know him as Nigantha Nataputta, proving that an organized Nigantha/Jain community was recognized by rival near-contemporary traditions.
stages.consequence: Nayaputta/Nataputta refers to Mahavira, not Buddha.
stages.trap: Mains/PYQ use: Biography answers should separate cross-tradition core, sect-specific detail and chronological caution.
stages.answer: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.

stages.title: JAIN ONTOLOGY: JIVA, AJIVA AND A LIVING COSMOS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Ajiva includes pudgala (matter), dharma as the medium of motion, adharma as the medium of rest, akasha (space) and, in common six-substance classification, kala (time).
stages.mechanism: FACT: Ajiva includes pudgala (matter), dharma as the medium of motion, adharma as the medium of rest, akasha (space) and, in common six-substance classification, kala (time).
stages.consequence: Mains/PYQ use: Link the broad ontology of life directly to dietary, occupational and monastic ethics, then state the category limit.
stages.trap: QUALIFICATION: Modern biological categories should not be projected onto this religious ontology.
stages.answer: FACT: Jiva is conscious, potentially omniscient and capable of liberation; embodied jivas occupy many grades of sense-capacity.

stages.title: JAIN KARMA, BONDAGE AND LIBERATION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Jain karma is subtle material matter that adheres to the soul because of activity and passions.
stages.mechanism: Jain karma is subtle material matter that adheres to the soul because of activity and passions.
stages.consequence: FACT: Liberation reveals the jiva's inherent knowledge, perception, bliss and energy; it does not merge into a creator god.
stages.trap: Jain karma is not merely metaphorical moral memory.
stages.answer: FACT: Asrava is karmic influx; bandha is bondage; samvara stops new influx; nirjara sheds accumulated karma; moksha is the liberated state.

stages.title: JAIN TRIRATNA, FIVE VOWS AND ASCETIC-LAY PATHS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: QUALIFICATION: Ahimsa does not make historical Jain communities economically or politically identical; practice varied by region, sect and occupation.
stages.mechanism: QUALIFICATION: Ahimsa does not make historical Jain communities economically or politically identical; practice varied by region, sect and occupation.
stages.consequence: Correct: That is the Buddhist three refuges, not the Jain path triad.
stages.trap: FACT: The five vows are ahimsa, satya, asteya, brahmacharya and aparigraha.
stages.answer: The five vows are absolute mahavratas for ascetics and limited anuvratas for householders, creating a demanding but socially sustainable two-level discipline.

stages.title: ANEKANTAVADA, SYADVADA AND NAYAVADA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Anekantavada is an ontological/epistemic warning against reducing a complex object to one absolute description.
stages.consequence: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.trap: FACT: Saptabhangi uses combinations of is, is not and is inexpressible under specified standpoints.
stages.answer: Anekantavada is the doctrine that reality has many aspects; nayavada analyzes partial standpoints; syadvada expresses qualified predication, conventionally through seven possible formulations.

stages.title: JAIN SANGHA, WOMEN, SOCIAL ETHICS AND LIMITS — [CORE MAINS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: FACT: Shvetambara tradition recognizes women's capacity for liberation and identifies Malli as a female Tirthankara; Digambara doctrine generally requires male rebirth for final liberation.
stages.mechanism: Mains/PYQ use: A social answer should pair widened religious agency with sectarian and societal limits.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Merchant support suited a mobile mendicant order and an ethic of trust, restraint and donation, but the tradition was not only mercantile.
stages.trap: Religious access does not equal modern social equality.
stages.answer: This widened participation, but access did not erase hierarchy, gender debates or the demanding ascetic definition of liberation.

stages.title: JAIN COUNCILS, CANON AND REDACTION TRADITIONS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Councils at Pataliputra and Valabhi are best presented as conventional redaction memories shaped by famine, migration, oral loss and sectarian authority.
stages.mechanism: Councils at Pataliputra and Valabhi are best presented as conventional redaction memories shaped by famine, migration, oral loss and sectarian authority.
stages.consequence: TRADITION: A Pataliputra council under Sthulabhadra is said to have collected surviving teachings; Digambara tradition does not accept that the original canon survived intact.
stages.trap: Digambaras do not accept the extant Shvetambara Agamas as the intact original canon.
stages.answer: Jain canonical history is reconstructed differently by Shvetambara and Digambara traditions.

stages.title: DIGAMBARA, SHVETAMBARA AND BOUNDED SUBSECT HISTORY — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Terapanth has distinct Shvetambara and Digambara usages; do not assume every similarly named subsect has one history.
stages.mechanism: The Digambara-Shvetambara division developed gradually and cannot be reduced to one famine or clothing dispute.
stages.consequence: FACT: Digambara means 'sky-clad' and Shvetambara 'white-clad'; clothing is visible but not the only distinction.
stages.trap: CAUTION: Its roots are linked to fifteenth-century Lonka Shah and later organization; the exact emergence should not be compressed into the ancient period.
stages.answer: FACT: Terapanth has distinct Shvetambara and Digambara usages; do not assume every similarly named subsect has one history.

stages.title: JAIN SPREAD, PATRONS, SITES, ART AND LITERATURE — [CORE PRELIMS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: FACT: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription and Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are major early Jain-linked evidence in Kalinga.
stages.mechanism: Wrong: Chandragupta's Jain migration is directly documented by a contemporary inscription.
stages.consequence: TRADITION/LIMIT: Shravanabelagola links Bhadrabahu and Chandragupta Maurya to southern migration, but the surviving epigraphic tradition is later and cannot independently prove every detail.
stages.trap: FACT: Kharavela's Hathigumpha inscription and Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are major early Jain-linked evidence in Kalinga.
stages.answer: Jain literature is multilingual and not confined to Ardhamagadhi.

stages.title: THE BUDDHA: HISTORICAL CORE AND TRADITIONAL LIFE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Ashoka's Rummindei pillar inscription provides early epigraphic association of Lumbini with the Buddha, centuries after his life but firmer than late biography alone.
stages.consequence: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.trap: LIMIT: Lalitavistara, Buddhacharita and later hagiographies are invaluable reception texts but not contemporaneous biographies.
stages.answer: The Buddha is historically located in the fifth-century BCE Gangetic world, while detailed biographies were shaped over centuries.

stages.title: FOUR NOBLE TRUTHS: DIAGNOSIS, CAUSE, CESSATION AND PATH — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Dukkha: Conditioned unsatisfactoriness Samudaya: Craving sustained by ignorance Nirodha: Cessation/release is possible Magga: Eightfold path.
stages.mechanism: Dukkha: Conditioned unsatisfactoriness Samudaya: Craving sustained by ignorance Nirodha: Cessation/release is possible Magga: Eightfold path.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: The medical analogy - diagnosis, cause, cure and treatment - captures structure but should not trivialize the existential claim.
stages.trap: The truths are a linked analysis, not four unrelated beliefs.
stages.answer: Pairs with the Middle Way discussion that follows; the four boxes are the diagnosis-cause-cure-path frame UPSC MCQs test most often.

stages.title: EIGHTFOLD PATH, MIDDLE WAY AND ETHICAL DISCIPLINE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Mains/PYQ use: A doctrine answer should group the eight factors and show their ethical/social implications.
stages.mechanism: Its eight factors are usually grouped into wisdom, ethical conduct and mental discipline; they are cultivated together rather than as a simple staircase.
stages.consequence: Correct: It is a disciplined soteriological path, not vague centrism.
stages.trap: Correct: It is an ethical path factor with lay implications, while monastic rules are more detailed.
stages.answer: QUALIFICATION: 'Middle Way' does not mean compromise between truth and falsehood; it concerns disciplined avoidance of spiritually fruitless extremes.

stages.title: DEPENDENT ORIGINATION: PROCESS WITHOUT A FIRST CAUSE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.mechanism: FACT: The teaching rejects both an unconditioned creator explanation for the cycle and a permanent self passing unchanged through it.
stages.consequence: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.trap: FACT: Craving is important but not isolated; ignorance, sense contact and clinging show a wider causal psychology.
stages.answer: Dependent origination is conditionality, not predestination.

stages.title: IMPERMANENCE, NO-SELF, AGGREGATES, KARMA AND NIRVANA — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Early Buddhism links impermanence (anicca), unsatisfactoriness (dukkha) and no-self (anatta).
stages.mechanism: Early Buddhism links impermanence (anicca), unsatisfactoriness (dukkha) and no-self (anatta).
stages.consequence: FACT: Karma is centrally intentional action (cetana) with ethical consequences; it is not Jain karmic matter.
stages.trap: FACT: Nirvana is extinction of greed, hatred and delusion and release from the conditioned cycle; it is not a heaven.
stages.answer: A person is analyzed as five changing aggregates; karmic continuity operates without an eternal atman.

stages.title: SANGHA, VINAYA, LAY SUPPORT AND INSTITUTIONAL LIFE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Monks and nuns followed Vinaya; lay donors supplied food, robes, medicine, dwellings and endowments in exchange for teaching, merit and social prestige.
stages.mechanism: Monks and nuns followed Vinaya; lay donors supplied food, robes, medicine, dwellings and endowments in exchange for teaching, merit and social prestige.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Monasteries linked routes, towns and courts, but they were not simply commercial corporations.
stages.trap: LIMIT: Textual ideals and inscriptional practice differ; donor labels do not reveal every motive.
stages.answer: FACT: Anathapindika's Jetavana and Visakha's patronage are prominent textual examples of wealthy lay support.

stages.title: WOMEN, SOCIAL ACCESS AND THE CASTE-VARNA QUESTION — [CORE MAINS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: FACT: Sangha admission across varna widened salvific access, but rules restricting debtors, slaves, soldiers or those under obligations reveal accommodation to social order.
stages.mechanism: Correct: It criticized birth superiority and widened access but did not erase social hierarchy.
stages.consequence: Buddhism widened access to renunciation and moral status, but it did not create modern equality or abolish caste society.
stages.trap: TRADITION: Mahapajapati Gotami's ordination marks the bhikkhuni order; the eight garudhammas are textually transmitted but their formation and dating are debated.
stages.answer: FACT: Sangha admission across varna widened salvific access, but rules restricting debtors, slaves, soldiers or those under obligations reveal accommodation to social order.

stages.title: BUDDHIST COUNCILS: CONVENTIONAL ACCOUNTS WITH SOURCE CAUTION — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: They should be learned for examinations but labelled by tradition because dates, patrons, participants and outcomes are not uniformly attested.
stages.mechanism: They should be learned for examinations but labelled by tradition because dates, patrons, participants and outcomes are not uniformly attested.
stages.consequence: Climb this ladder before answering an 'assess the councils' Mains question; each rung is a caveat to state, not a fact to assert.
stages.trap: LIMIT: Numbering conceals multiple regional memories; use 'conventional account' rather than certitude.
stages.answer: The second council is primarily a Vinaya dispute in conventional accounts.

stages.title: BUDDHIST CANONS: PALI, SANSKRIT, CHINESE AND TIBETAN WITNESSES — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada materials survive in Sanskrit fragments and especially Chinese/Tibetan translations; their Vinayas are not the Pali Vinaya.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Sarvastivada and Mulasarvastivada materials survive in Sanskrit fragments and especially Chinese/Tibetan translations; their Vinayas are not the Pali Vinaya.
stages.consequence: LIMIT: Pali is not simply the exact spoken language of the Buddha, Sanskrit is not exclusively Mahayana, and 'the Buddhist canon' is not singular.
stages.trap: Sanskrit use is not a sufficient test for Mahayana identity.
stages.answer: The Pali Tipitaka is the complete canon of the Theravada tradition; Sanskrit and Buddhist Hybrid Sanskrit texts preserve other schools and Mahayana currents; Chinese and Tibetan translations preserve many Indic works now lost in India.

stages.title: EARLY SCHOOLS AND THE THERAVADA-HINAYANA TERMINOLOGY FIREWALL — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Sthavira means 'elders' and Mahasanghika 'great community/assembly'; the first split is remembered differently by school sources.
stages.consequence: Modern Theravada is one surviving Sthavira-derived lineage, not a synonym for every early school.
stages.trap: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.answer: Sthavira and Mahasanghika are early broad lineages; Sarvastivada, Dharmaguptaka, Mahishasaka and others developed distinct Vinaya and Abhidharma traditions.

stages.title: MAHAYANA, THE BODHISATTVA PATH, MAITREYA AND PARAMITAS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Mahayana is not defined solely by Sanskrit or image worship.
stages.mechanism: Mahayana is not defined solely by Sanskrit or image worship.
stages.consequence: Maitreya is the future Buddha, not exclusively a Mahayana figure.
stages.trap: INTERPRETATION: Image worship, devotion and merit transfer widened modes of participation, but none alone defines every Mahayana community.
stages.answer: FACT: Maitreya is the future Buddha in both Theravada and Mahayana traditions; Mahayana also venerates him as a Bodhisattva in Tushita.

stages.title: MADHYAMAKA AND YOGACARA: BOUNDED HISTORICAL DEPTH — [CORE MAINS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: FACT: Yogacara is associated with Asanga and Vasubandhu and analyzes experience through consciousness/representation, including store consciousness in developed formulations.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Yogacara is associated with Asanga and Vasubandhu and analyzes experience through consciousness/representation, including store consciousness in developed formulations.
stages.consequence: LIMIT: 'Nothing exists' is an inaccurate summary of Madhyamaka; 'only my mind exists' is an oversimplification of Yogacara.
stages.trap: FACT: The two truths framework distinguishes conventional and ultimate truth; emptiness itself is not a substance.
stages.answer: For Ancient History, Madhyamaka and Yogacara should be treated as major Mahayana scholastic developments, not turned into an optional-level metaphysics essay.

stages.title: VAJRAYANA: LATER TANTRIC DEVELOPMENT AND INSTITUTIONAL SETTING — [CORE MAINS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.mechanism: Vajrayana developed within later Mahayana environments, especially from the mid-first millennium CE onward.
stages.consequence: Mains/PYQ use: Present Vajrayana as transformation within Buddhist history, not a moralized endpoint.
stages.trap: LIMIT: Older textbook narratives that reduce decline to corrupt Vajrayana practice are polemical and monocausal.
stages.answer: FACT: Vajrayana is not the Buddha's original sixth-century BCE institutional form; its major textual and ritual systems are later.

stages.title: WHY THE TRADITIONS BECAME POPULAR: LANGUAGE, ETHICS AND NETWORKS
stages.terms: FACT: Buddhist monasteries could travel and reproduce through ordination lineages; Jain ascetics and lay communities built durable regional circuits.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Buddhist monasteries could travel and reproduce through ordination lineages; Jain ascetics and lay communities built durable regional circuits.
stages.consequence: INTERPRETATION: Buddhism's Middle Way may have eased recruitment compared with rigorous Jain ascetic ideals, while Jain anuvratas enabled strong lay continuity.
stages.trap: LIMIT: 'Buddhism spread because it was simple' ignores complex doctrine; 'Jainism failed to spread' ignores its extensive regional history.
stages.answer: Language choice aided communication but does not prove mass literacy.

stages.title: PATRONAGE NETWORKS: MAURYAN AND POST-MAURYAN WORLDS — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Sanchi's brick stupa, pillar and later enlargements show Mauryan inception followed by Shunga, Satavahana and other patronage.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Sanchi's brick stupa, pillar and later enlargements show Mauryan inception followed by Shunga, Satavahana and other patronage.
stages.consequence: Correct: His edicts promote dhamma and sect respect; Buddhist patronage does not equal coercive establishment.
stages.trap: Read the structure first; each arrow is a historical relationship, not an automatic law.
stages.answer: Ashoka is central but not the sole patron; post-Mauryan regional states, monks, nuns, merchants and artisans made Buddhism materially durable, while Jainism grew through different regional coalitions.

stages.title: REGIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL SPREAD: A TEXT MAP — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: Buddhism became a trans-Asian network through multiple routes and translations; Jainism achieved durable but more regionally concentrated expansion within India.
stages.mechanism: Mains/PYQ use: Use routes, carriers, texts and sites, then add chronology control.
stages.consequence: Spread was not a single outward wave from one centre.
stages.trap: Treat the arrows as relationships worth remembering, not as directions or distances; the prose names the actual regions and routes.
stages.answer: Buddhism became a trans-Asian network through multiple routes and translations; Jainism achieved durable but more regionally concentrated expansion within India.

stages.title: STUPAS, CAVES, MONASTERIES, IMAGES AND MATERIAL EVIDENCE — [CORE PRELIMS + CORE MAINS]
stages.terms: FACT: Jain material evidence includes Kankali Tila, Udayagiri-Khandagiri, Ellora Jain caves and later temple/manuscript traditions.
stages.mechanism: FACT: Barabar caves were donated by Ashoka and Dasharatha to Ajivikas, a reminder that rock-cut architecture is not only Buddhist.
stages.consequence: They cannot by themselves identify a text or prove a traditional biography, but inscriptions and stratigraphy can date institutions more firmly.
stages.trap: Mains/PYQ use: Use form + named site + donor/inscription + inference + limit.
stages.answer: FACT: Stupas developed as relic, commemorative and votive monuments; the concept was not exclusively Buddhist in origin, although Buddhism transformed it extensively.

stages.title: JAINISM AND BUDDHISM: A CONTROLLED COMPARISON
stages.terms: Mains/PYQ use: A high-scoring comparison moves dimension by dimension and ends with shared context plus divergent solutions.
stages.mechanism: Mains/PYQ use: A high-scoring comparison moves dimension by dimension and ends with shared context plus divergent solutions.
stages.consequence: FACT: Both use monastic-lay reciprocity, but Buddhist institutions achieved wider trans-Asian monastic expansion while Jain networks remained more India-centred and lay-dense.
stages.trap: QUALIFICATION: 'Jain extreme versus Buddhist moderate' is a starting contrast, not a complete history; both traditions contain varied disciplines and later devotional forms.
stages.answer: FACT: Jain karma is subtle matter binding jiva; Buddhist karma is intentional action within causal continuity.

stages.title: BUDDHISM'S DECLINE AND TRANSFORMATION IN INDIA
stages.terms: Turkish attacks are a late factor, not the single cause.
stages.mechanism: Turkish attacks are a late factor, not the single cause.
stages.consequence: Its institutional contraction was regionally uneven and multi-causal, while doctrines, images, pilgrimage and communities persisted or were absorbed into new configurations.
stages.trap: LIMIT: Older narratives blaming luxury, women, Sanskrit or Turks alone are reductive and sometimes polemical.
stages.answer: FACT: Raids and warfare damaged major institutions such as Nalanda and Vikramashila, but attacks cannot explain centuries of earlier regional decline or transformation.

stages.title: WHY JAINISM PERSISTED AND HOW IT TRANSFORMED
stages.terms: Trace every arrow before drafting the Mains answer on Buddhism's transformation; no single box should be quoted alone as 'the' cause.
stages.mechanism: Trace every arrow before drafting the Mains answer on Buddhism's transformation; no single box should be quoted alone as 'the' cause.
stages.consequence: LIMIT: Jain history also includes decline in some regions, sectarian conflict, social accommodation and changes in patronage; continuity is not stasis.
stages.trap: Persistence should not be explained only by merchant wealth.
stages.answer: Mains/PYQ use: Compare distributed lay institutions with concentrated Buddhist mahaviharas, but avoid a deterministic contrast.

stages.title: HISTORIOGRAPHY AND EVIDENCE LIMITS — [CORE MAINS + SUPPORTING]
stages.terms: Mains/PYQ use: Every evidence paragraph should finish with the source's genre and reach.
stages.mechanism: Wrong: An inscription is unbiased because it is contemporary.
stages.consequence: FACT: Ashokan edicts, donor inscriptions and Hathigumpha provide firmer dated anchors but rarely explain doctrine comprehensively.
stages.trap: FACT: Art can reveal patronage, ritual and iconography, but aniconic symbols do not automatically identify one event without context.
stages.answer: The history of Jainism and Buddhism is reconstructed from normative texts, rival accounts, inscriptions, monuments, art, manuscripts and later chronicles.

stages.title: CONTEMPORARY HERITAGE AND CONSERVATION LINKAGES
stages.terms: RETRIEVED FACT: UNESCO describes Nalanda's surviving viharas, temples and art as evidence of a long monastic-scholastic institution and notes conservation by ASI.
stages.mechanism: RETRIEVED FACT: UNESCO describes Nalanda's surviving viharas, temples and art as evidence of a long monastic-scholastic institution and notes conservation by ASI.
stages.consequence: INFERENCE: Heritage management today preserves evidence of Buddhist institutional transformation; it does not settle doctrinal authenticity.
stages.trap: UNESCO listing is a modern heritage status, not ancient evidence by itself.
stages.answer: Mains/PYQ use: Use heritage only as a final contemporary linkage after the ancient evidence is complete.

stages.title: CHRONOLOGY, TERMINOLOGY AND RAPID UPSC DISTINCTIONS
stages.terms: Mains/PYQ use: Use this card to audit terminology before finalizing any answer.
stages.mechanism: Mains/PYQ use: Use this card to audit terminology before finalizing any answer.
stages.consequence: Wrong: Sanghabhuti and Sanghabhadra are variants of one name.
stages.trap: Correct: They are different historical monks/scholars.
stages.answer: Council accounts are conventional and tradition-specific.
